prompt:
Photorealistic cinematic documentary travel photograph, 35mm lens, natural film grain, rich fine detail, authentic and unposed. Dusk on a narrow stone-paved lane in Kyoto's Higashiyama district. The five-story Yasaka Pagoda rises at the end of the lane above low, dark wooden machiya townhouses with tiled eaves. Paper lanterns glow warmly along the lane as the only warm accent. Deep indigo and navy palette with one thin peach-coral glow in the sky directly behind the pagoda, silhouetting its tiered roofs.

Composition, square 1:1 frame, centered: the pagoda is on the vertical center line, its tip at about 18% down and its base at about 62% down, the lane leading to it from the bottom of the frame, the machiya rooflines forming dark diagonals on both sides. All important subject matter stays inside the central 70% of the frame height. The top-right quarter is calm, dark, empty indigo sky with no bright highlights. The bottom 15% is dark, simple stone paving with a faint lantern reflection. No readable text, no signage, no logos, no watermarks, no people.
